# FairMedFM

> Fairness evaluation for any binary classification or segmentation model. `pip install fairmedfm` computes subgroup AUC, accuracy, calibration (ECE) and cross-entropy gaps, equal opportunity, equalized odds and Dice disparities from per-sample predictions and a sensitive attribute such as sex, age or race. It is also the FairMedFM benchmark of 20 medical imaging foundation models on 17 datasets (arXiv:2407.00983).

The pip package depends only on NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn (no PyTorch or GPU) and reproduces the metrics used in the FairMedFM paper. Command line: `fairmedfm score --task cls --input predictions.csv --sensitive sex age` or `fairmedfm score --task seg --input dice.csv --sensitive sex`. Python: `fairmedfm.classification_fairness(prob, label, group)` and `fairmedfm.segmentation_fairness(dice, group)`. To run the benchmark with built-in foundation models, install `fairmedfm[cls]` (classification) or `fairmedfm[seg]` (segmentation) and use `fairmedfm run`.

## Key facts

### Can I use FairMedFM to evaluate my own model?

Yes. Any binary classifier or segmentation model works, in medical imaging or any other domain. Run the model anywhere, save one row per sample (classification: positive-class probability, 0/1 label, sensitive attributes; segmentation: Dice score, sensitive attributes) and run `fairmedfm score`. The model does not need to be one of the FairMedFM foundation models.

### Which fairness metrics does the pip package compute for classification?

overall-auc, overall-acc, overall-bce and overall-ece on all samples; worst-auc (lowest group AUC); auc-gap, acc-gap, bce-gap and ece-gap (largest minus smallest group value); eo, the equal opportunity gap (largest minus smallest group true positive rate); and eod, an equalized odds score defined as 1 - (TPR gap + TNR gap) / 2, where 1 means equal rates. Accuracy, eo and eod use the threshold with the best overall F1. Per-group values are reported at threshold 0.5 and at the best-F1 threshold. ECE uses 10 equal-width bins over the range of the predicted probabilities.

### Which fairness metrics does it compute for segmentation?

mean_dice over all samples; min_dice and max_dice (worst and best group mean Dice); delta_dice (their difference); std_dice (standard deviation of the group means); skewness_dice ((1 - min_dice) / (1 - max_dice)); and es_dice, the equity-scaled Dice mean_dice / (1 + std_dice).

### What inputs are supported?

Sensitive attributes with two or more groups, given as strings or integers. Classification labels must be binary and every group needs positive and negative samples. Multi-class classification is not supported yet; evaluate each class one-vs-rest. Python 3.10 to 3.13.

### What does the FairMedFM benchmark cover?

The paper evaluates 20 foundation models on 17 medical imaging datasets (including CheXpert, MIMIC-CXR, HAM10000, PAPILA, FairVLMed10k, GF3300, ADNI, TUSC and FairSeg) with linear probing, zero-shot, CLIP adaptation, parameter-efficient fine-tuning and prompted segmentation, and compares unfairness mitigation methods. The repository has since added newer models such as DINOv3, SigLIP2, AIMv2, MedGemma, RETFound, UNI2-h, Virchow2, Prov-GigaPath, CONCH, Merlin, SAM2, SAM3 and MedicalSAM3. The benchmark runs with `pip install "fairmedfm[cls]"` or `"fairmedfm[seg]"` and `fairmedfm run`, or from the GitHub repository with `python main.py` in the paper's environment.

### What did the FairMedFM benchmark find?

All evaluated medical foundation models show fairness disparities across sex, race and age; the most accurate model is often not the fairest; disparities on a dataset stay similar across models; and existing unfairness mitigation methods give only marginal improvements.
